_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.
_meta.maintenance: Manual updates + Claude WebSearch each session. 2026-07-28 refresh: Iran/US fighting paused Jul 27 at Iran's request (Brent -11.3% to $85.87 — biggest single-day drop since Apr 8, but level still elevated); Warsh Fed remains hawkish with 5th consecutive hold expected + 9/18 members forecast at least one hike this year; USMCA joint review opened Jul 1 with Section 122 10% Mexico surcharge expiring ~Jul 24 (renewal decision imminent).

themes.title: US-Iran active fighting paused Jul 27 — Brent -11.3% but still elevated, Hormuz traffic thin
themes.summary: US halted strikes on Iran Jul 27 at Iran's request after ~2 weeks of active fighting that collapsed the 60-day ceasefire. Trump warned strikes resume if new ceasefire deal isn't reached — this is a PAUSE, not resolution. Brent closed $85.87 Jul 27 (-11.3%, biggest single-day drop since Apr 8) but remains historically elevated. Strait of Hormuz shipping still catastrophically low: <10 vessels/day vs ~100 pre-war. Houthi Red Sea threat still active on Saudi tankers. Two-sided regime: risk-off UNWIND (haven trades bleeding) vs residual supply premium in oil. Trades that were correct in escalation phase (long JPY/CHF, long CAD via oil) are now the loser side if pause holds.

implications.CAD: WEAKENING tailwind — oil premium unwinding as Brent slides toward $80s. Still supported if Hormuz stays constrained, but the pure crisis bid is gone. Trim aggressive long-CAD exposure.
implications.JPY: haven bid FADING — risk-off unwinding, JPY strength driver weakening. Bearish JPY if pause holds.
implications.CHF: haven bid FADING — same story as JPY. CHF crosses that were long-CHF start reversing.
implications.USD: haven premium unwinding — DXY was elevated on crisis bid, that's now leaking out. Neutral USD.
implications.AUD: TAILWIND returning — risk-off compression lifting, high-beta / commodity currencies get relief bid
implications.NZD: TAILWIND returning — same as AUD, risk-on rotation
implications.GBP: neutral — was mixed during escalation, less directly affected either way

themes.watchLevel: Brent >$88 = pause breaking, escalation resuming (revert to prior playbook). Brent <$78 = full de-escalation priced in, drop all haven premium. Hormuz traffic recovery to >30 vessels/day = supply premium collapses further.

themes.title: Warsh Fed hawkish — 5th consecutive hold expected, 9/18 forecast a 2026 hike
themes.summary: Kevin Warsh (Fed Chair since May) sticking with hawkish framing at July FOMC. Rates held 3.5-3.75% for fifth straight meeting. June CPI declined -0.4% m/m taking annual to 3.5% (from 4.2% May) — cooling but Warsh has explicitly said FOMC has 'no tolerance for persistently elevated inflation.' Median year-end 2026 rate forecast raised to 3.8% (from 3.4%); 9 of 18 members now expect at least one hike this year. Traditional forward guidance eliminated — pure data-dependent. Net: USD carry stays firm, hike risk is one-sided (higher, not lower).

implications.USD: STRUCTURAL tailwind — hawkish Warsh + hike-tilted dots = USD carry defended
implications.JPY: STRUCTURAL headwind — persistent carry gap; BoJ still ultra-loose relative to Fed
implications.EUR: headwind — ECB cutting while Fed holds hawkish widens rate diff against EUR
implications.GBP: headwind — BoE also cutting; USD carry differential works vs GBP too
implications.CAD: mixed — USD strength offsets oil support; USDCAD structurally biased up unless oil rerates
implications.AUD: headwind — RBA on hold with easing bias; carry disadvantaged vs USD

themes.watchLevel: Any hint of Warsh softening in speeches = pivot back in play, unwinds this theme. Sub-3.0% Y/Y CPI print = dovish tolerance returns. DXY closing below 100 = market rejecting hawkish read.

themes.title: USMCA review live + Section 122 Mexico surcharge expires ~Jul 24 — binary event
themes.summary: Two live threads. (1) USMCA joint review opened Jul 1 — Trump said 'not renewing in current form.' First US-Mexico bilateral round done May, tackled auto rules of origin + steel/alu + economic security. (2) Section 122 10% Mexico surcharge (imposed after SCOTUS struck down IEEPA tariffs Feb 20) expires ~Jul 24 by 150-day statutory limit — 15% version announced but no formal proclamation. Extension mechanism, replacement action, or lapse each move CAD/MXN differently. Result: CAD trades in a headline-driven regime with binary risk that could hit within days.

implications.CAD: elevated vol BOTH directions — surcharge lapse/extend + USMCA framing decisions land in a compressed window. Wider SLs, smaller sizes on CAD-crosses.
implications.USD: moderate vol — indirect via trade-policy narrative; less directly hit than CAD/MXN
implications.MXN: highest exposure (not in book) — but MXN moves telegraph CAD next-day

themes.watchLevel: Section 122 formal extension proclamation OR clean lapse resolves half the theme. USMCA renewal terms announcement resolves the other half. Watch for USDMXN / USDCAD gaps on any Trump trade-policy speech.
